junction.name: Aurora Avenue North & North 105th Street, Seattle

claims.text: Aurora Avenue North & North 105th Street had 63 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 2 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.3 million a year.
6% of crashes here were recorded as “from same direction - both going straight - one stopped - sideswipe” crashes, against 1% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 1.4 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: national studies only), worth $472,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.9 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $647,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for Aurora Avenue North (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for North 104th Street, North 105th Street, North Northgate Way (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) and the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
